text: The liberation of the hand. <break time="0.8s" /> From its primarily walking related function. <break time="0.8s" /> Made possible a massive diversification of images. <break time="0.8s" /> Through digital movement and grasping. <break time="0.8s" /> This in turn allowed for an explosion. <break time="0.8s" /> In the diversity and function of tools. <break time="0.8s" /> That could be manipulated by the hand. <break time="0.8s" /> Including gesture or graphism. <break time="0.8s" /> The manipulation of matter with the hand. <break time="0.8s" /> Gesture and graphism thus increasingly enabled. <break time="0.8s" /> The gathering or centripetal contraction. <break time="0.8s" /> Of an extremely wide diversity. <break time="0.8s" /> Of rhythmic motions of the arm and hand. <break time="0.8s" /> The freedom of the hand. <break time="0.8s" /> Not only made possible an increased kinetic capacity. <break time="0.8s" /> For grasping and accumulating things toward the center of the body. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as putting food into the mouth. <break time="0.8s" /> But it also permitted a rhythmic accumulation of natural motions. <break time="0.8s" /> In the arm and hand itself. <break time="0.8s" /> Like the repetitive motion of striking stones to make tools. <break time="0.8s" /> In other words. <break time="0.8s" /> The hand began to reflect certain natural motions. <break time="0.8s" /> Waves, wind, water, and so on in the functional graphic patterns or distribution of images. <break time="0.8s" /> That define the aesthetic field.
